text.arabic_uthmani: وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُۥ وَهُوَ ظَالِمٌۭ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ قَالَ مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدًۭا

words.gloss_range: ayah-opening connector that resumes and carries the prior narrative into a new action beat
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the ayah attached to the preceding boast instead of starting a detached episode. The small connector moves the parable from prior speech into embodied entry, so the wealth claim from 18:34 is carried forward into the scene where it will be exposed.

topics.headline: continuation from boast into bodily action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not reset the story; it carries the owner's boast from 18:34 into the physical act of entering.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as linking or resumptive, and the local clause begins the entry scene, so the CRITICAL continuation rows survive.

words.gloss_range: completed Form I entry into the garden as a direct object-domain
words.root_gloss_range: entry, going inside, insertion, inclusion, and a related hidden-flaw branch; local grammar selects physical entry while allowing internal-flaw pressure only as coloring
words.prose: {{ar:دَخَلَ}} ({{tr:dakhala}}) makes the owner actively cross into the garden as a completed scene event. Because the garden is its direct object, the property becomes an entered domain, and the following circumstantial clause immediately turns that crossing into a diagnosed moral scene. The root's hidden-flaw branch is only background coloring, but it fits the local fact that the entry is accompanied by self-wronging. The same entry language later returns as direct address at 18:39, so the reported act here is replayed as accountability.

topics.headline: active entry into an owned domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the man is not merely near or speaking about the garden; he actively crosses into the very domain he claims.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence makes the garden the direct object of the Form I perfect verb, supporting active entry into a spatial object-domain.

topics.headline: completed entry before moral diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the perfect verb lets the entry land as a completed act while the following state clause carries the continuing moral diagnosis.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a perfect 3ms Form I verb, and the circumstantial attachment licenses the entry-to-diagnosis hinge.

topics.headline: entry colored by internal flaw
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entry is not morally neutral; the root field can suggest an inward flaw while local grammar still selects physical entry.
topics.reason: The physical entry sense is locally selected by the direct object, so the hidden-flaw branch remains a bounded lexical pressure rather than the local sense.

topics.headline: entry returns as direct rebuke
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reported entry here is later replayed in direct address at 18:39, turning the same action into accountability.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give a concrete same-surah recurrence at 18:39, and nothing in the guardrails blocks using it as a later rebuke parallel.

topics.headline: clipped entry sound
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The sound observation is plausible but adds no distinct reader-facing lexical or structural payoff beyond the retained entry-domain topic.
topics.reason: The row is accounted for, but its payoff is mainly acoustic decoration after the stronger grammatical and recurrence topics are retained.

words.gloss_range: his garden as a possessed, definite, singular, accusative object-domain
words.root_gloss_range: covering and concealment, tree-covered garden, hidden afterlife garden, hidden beings, inner concealment, and related mental-covering branches; local sense is the owned garden branch

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the later feminine demonstrative pointing back to the entered garden

words.prose: {{ar:جَنَّتَهُۥ}} ({{tr:jannatahu}}) names the garden as a singular possessed object: identifiable through his suffix, not through a generic article. The accusative role makes it the domain entered, and later {{ar:هَٰذِهِۦٓ}} ({{tr:hādhihi}}) points back to the same garden as the thing he says will not perish. The singular form compresses the earlier abundance of gardens in 18:32-33 into one owned space he can enter and point at. The concealment field of {{ar:ج ن ن}} ({{tr:j-n-n}}) is narrowed to the garden sense here, but it still makes the owned property feel like an enclosed self-world beside the explicit self-wronging; the same-surah contrast at 18:50 keeps garden, hidden-being, and wronging fields in view without changing the local garden sense.

topics.headline: ownership built into the garden word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the garden is made definite by his possession, so ownership is built into the word before the boast is spoken.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the 3ms possessive suffix and its antecedent, preserving the ownership and definiteness claims.

topics.headline: entered object becomes pointed subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the garden first functions as the object crossed into and then returns through the demonstrative as the subject of the denied perishing.
topics.reason: The direct-object attachment for word 3 and demonstrative-reference evidence for word 14 jointly license the object-to-subject architecture.

topics.headline: garden branch with concealment pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the locally selected garden can still feel like a covered interior, matching the ayah's movement from owned enclosure to damaged self.
topics.reason: V4 confirms separate covering and tree-covered garden branches, so the local sense remains garden while concealment survives as root-image pressure.

topics.headline: abundance narrowed to one claimed garden
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that earlier garden abundance in 18:32-33 is compressed into one possessed garden he can enter and point at.
topics.reason: The local form is singular with a possessive suffix, and the cited parable recurrence gives a concrete abundance-to-owned-instance movement.

topics.headline: private garden against larger garden fields
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owner's private garden touches wider Quranic garden and wrongdoing fields, including the same-surah root contrast at 18:50.
topics.reason: The rows use concrete references and do not replace the local garden sense, so they survive as controlled intertextual and field contrasts.

topics.reason: The row is recorded as acoustic filler after its strongest interpretive value is already covered by the enclosure topic.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial connector introducing the state that accompanies entry
words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge into a circumstantial clause. It makes the narrator's diagnosis simultaneous with the entry: the owner enters while already in the state named by the clause, rather than entering first and only later becoming wrong.

topics.headline: entry interpreted as accompanying state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wronging is folded into the act of entry itself, not added as a later event.
topics.reason: QAC explicitly identifies the particle as circumstantial, and the attachment evidence ties the clause to the entry verb.

words.gloss_range: independent 3ms pronoun serving as the subject of the circumstantial nominal clause
words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) keeps the entrant himself in view before the predicate lands. The independent pronoun gives the circumstantial clause a nominal, identifying shape, so the narrator is not merely reporting another action but holding the same owner before the label of wronging. It also marks a voice boundary: the narrator frames him from outside before the owner's first-person denial returns.

topics.headline: same actor held before judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entrant is explicitly held in focus as the one who carries the moral predicate.
topics.reason: The pronoun is an independent subject of the nominal circumstantial clause and refers to the same man who entered.

topics.headline: state, not new action

topics.reason: The clause is nominal inside the circumstantial frame, supporting a characterizing state.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a voice boundary: the narrator names him from outside before the man's first-person denial returns.
topics.reason: The third-person pronoun belongs to narrator framing before the first-person quote begins at the cognition verb.

words.gloss_range: active participial predicate naming him as a self-wronger inside the circumstantial clause
words.root_gloss_range: wronging, putting something out of its proper place, injustice, and darkness; local phrase specifies the wronging as directed to his own self

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the later first-person cognition verb whose denial demonstrates the diagnosis

words.prose: {{ar:ظَالِمٌ}} ({{tr:ẓālimun}}) is the narrator's predicate for the entrant, not a loose adjective. Its participial form makes wronging a present state, and the following phrase directs that wronging inward. The narrator gives this verdict before the quoted speech, so the denial that follows functions as proof of the diagnosis. The root's displacement and darkness range makes the later {{ar:أَظُنُّ}} ({{tr:aẓunnu}}) sound like cognition already darkened by self-displacement, while the grammar keeps the label in the nominal circumstantial clause. The phrase also belongs to a wider self-wronging field and scales within Surah 18 from garden yield at 18:33 to wider wrongdoers at 18:50.

topics.headline: nominative predicate in the state clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word is a nominative predicate identifying the entrant's state, not an object or detached adjective.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as the predicate of the independent pronoun in the circumstantial nominal clause.

topics.headline: active wronging as inward displacement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wrong is an ongoing self-displacement simultaneous with entry, not only a past moral mistake.
topics.reason: The active participle, circumstantial attachment, and following self-directed complement support an ongoing inward wronging.

topics.headline: wronging darkens estimation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the narrator's moral label and the man's later estimation are linked by both sense and sound, making the denial a cognitive symptom of wronging.
topics.reason: The rows connect wrongdoing, darkness, and estimation without confusing the distinct roots of the two words.

topics.headline: self-wronger within a larger wronging thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this phrase belongs to a recognized self-wronging field and also scales within Surah 18 from garden yield at 18:33 to wider wrongdoers at 18:50.
topics.reason: The cited formula and same-surah references are concrete and do not override the local parse.

topics.headline: verdict placed before the quoted proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the narrator gives the diagnosis before the owner's speech supplies the proof of it.
topics.reason: The clause order places the moral predicate before the quoted denial introduced by the speech verb.

words.gloss_range: prepositional lām directing and specifying the wronging toward the self
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) is the small preposition that routes the wronging inward. It governs the self-word and attaches the moral predicate to its harmed target, so the phrase does not leave wronging abstract; it specifies the damage as self-directed.

topics.headline: wronging routed toward the self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a tiny preposition turns the moral label into inward harm aimed at the man's own self.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the preposition as governing the self-word and functioning as the complement of the wronging predicate.

topics.headline: particle sound binds to self-word
topics.reason: The row's only distinct payoff is already preserved by the prepositional-fusion and inward-direction topic.

words.gloss_range: his own self, soul, person, or inner life as the governed target of wronging
words.root_gloss_range: self, soul, person, desire, breath, blood, vitality, and valued inner life; local phrase selects the possessed self as harmed target
words.prose: {{ar:نَفْسِهِ}} ({{tr:nafsihi}}) makes the harmed target personal: his own self, not an outside victim and not generic humanity. The genitive and suffix bind the self to the same owner whose garden was also marked as his, creating a sharp irony between outward possession and inward damage after the outward force boasted in 18:34. The root's range of self, breath, desire, and living personhood widens what is harmed without dislodging the local governed-object role. The phrase also enters a wider self-wronging formula, including the close classification at 35:32, and a Surah 18 self-thread running from restraint at 18:28 to protected life at 18:74.

topics.headline: his own self as the governed target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the damage is routed back into the same man's own self, marked by the possessive suffix.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the genitive self-word, and the suffix is linked to the same garden owner.

topics.headline: self, breath, desire, and living identity

topics.reason: The broad root range is meaningful, but local syntax narrows it to the possessed self governed by the preposition.

topics.reason: The local suffix and the cited previous-ayah contrast support the reversal without adding a new referent.

words.gloss_range: completed speech verb introducing direct quotation as the evidence of the prior diagnosis
words.root_gloss_range: saying, uttering, expressing meaning, and speech-act framing; local Form I perfect opens the owner's quoted claim
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) turns the narrator's diagnosis into audible evidence. The verb is a completed third-person speech frame with the same owner as implicit subject, and its quoted complement begins immediately with the denial. It externalizes an inner estimate as a performed utterance rather than leaving the wronging merely narrated. After the reciprocal conversation of 18:34, the simple saying narrows the exchange into the owner's one-sided first-person claim, and this speech frame opens a denial sequence that continues into 18:36 among the parable's rival claims.

topics.headline: speech supplies the proof of the diagnosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quoted denial is not narrator explanation; it is the speech evidence for the self-wronging just named.
topics.reason: The attachment bundle identifies the following utterance as the quoted complement of the speech verb.

topics.headline: same actor carried into speech

topics.reason: The verb's 3ms subject is implicit and recoverable from the preceding owner.

topics.headline: cognition becomes public assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owner's inward estimate becomes an uttered claim that performs denial in the scene.
topics.reason: The speech verb locally externalizes the quoted cognition clause rather than merely describing an opinion.

topics.headline: conversation collapses into one-sided saying
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from reciprocal exchange in 18:34 to a framed first-person monologue here.
topics.reason: The rows give a concrete prior conversation frame at 18:34, while the local form is simple Form I saying.

topics.headline: speech frame extends through the parable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this speech verb opens a denial sequence that continues into 18:36 and belongs to the parable's chain of rival claims.
topics.reason: The quoted complement begins here and contextual evidence supports a speech sequence extending beyond the ayah.

topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The acoustic row adds little after the speech-frame and denial-sequence topics preserve the structural payoff.
topics.reason: Recorded as acoustic filler.

words.gloss_range: negative particle scoping over the present cognition verb inside quoted speech
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the quoted denial by negating the speaker's present act of estimation. It is the negative particle here, not a question or relative marker, and together with the final temporal adverb it turns the possible perishing of the garden into a future that he refuses to admit.

topics.headline: denial scopes over estimating
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation first targets the speaker's estimation, before the perishing event is named as its content.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as negative, and translation support says the negation scopes over the cognition verb.

topics.headline: negation reaches toward no future opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening negation and the closing time word work together to leave no admitted future moment for the garden's perishing.
topics.reason: The final temporal adverb modifies the perishing event under the negative cognition frame.

words.gloss_range: first-person present estimation, supposing, conjecturing, or claiming certainty under negation
words.root_gloss_range: thinking, supposing, conjecture, suspicion, and at times certainty; local negated form keeps the epistemic range tense inside the owner's quote

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the narrator's prior wronging predicate that echoes the cognition verb
the negative particle governing the present cognition clause

words.prose: {{ar:أَظُنُّ}} ({{tr:aẓunnu}}) puts the boast in the owner's own present cognition: he says what he does not suppose, estimate, or hold as certain about the garden's perishing. The verb remains indicative under {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) and governs the subordinate perishing clause, so the loss remains inside a fully formed present mental frame. Because {{ar:ظ ن ن}} ({{tr:ẓ-n-n}}) ranges between conjecture and certainty, the negated claim is unstable rather than humble; it performs refusal to recognize perishability while echoing the narrator's prior {{ar:ظَالِمٌ}} ({{tr:ẓālimun}}) by sound and theme. The estimation thread continues into 18:36, contrasts with recognition in 21:87, and can be heard beside another arrogant estimation scene at 17:101-102.

topics.headline: present first-person estimate governs the loss clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the perishing of the garden is framed as the content of the speaker's present estimation, not as narrator assertion.
topics.reason: The verb is imperfect 1cs and governs the subordinate content complement.

topics.headline: negated without being made jussive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negative particle leaves the present cognitive stance fully formed rather than turning it into a different lam-negated construction.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the verb as indicative under the negative particle.

topics.headline: conjecture and certainty tense under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claim wavers between denying conjecture and denying certainty, which makes the speaker's confidence epistemically evasive.
topics.reason: The root range is valid, but the local grammar narrows it to a negated cognition verb taking the perishing clause as content.

topics.headline: faulty estimate echoes wronging
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker's estimating verb is tied to the narrator's wronging label by sound and moral-cognitive sequence.
topics.reason: The rows preserve a sound-and-theme link while keeping the two roots distinct.

topics.headline: estimation thread moves beyond this ayah

topics.reason: The concrete references are valid as contrast and sequence evidence, not as replacement for the local cognition parse.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive content particle turning the perishing verb into the cognition complement
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) keeps the perishing event inside the speaker's thought-frame. It governs the following subjunctive verb and makes the possible perishing a content proposition under the negated estimate, not an independently narrated event.

topics.headline: perishing made thinkable under negated estimation

topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the particle the head of the content complement and the governor of the subjunctive verb.

topics.headline: possible event placed under mood government
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle grammatically casts perishing as a dependent possibility before the speaker rejects it.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the particle's subjunctive governance.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive 3fs verb of perishing, vanishing, or becoming extinct, governed by the content particle and agreeing with the garden demonstrative
words.root_gloss_range: perishing away, coming to ruin, annihilating, and the related open-waste or desert branch; local verb selects total cessation under a negated cognition frame

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the content particle governing the subjunctive perishing verb
the negative particle that negates the speaker's estimation

words.prose: {{ar:تَبِيدَ}} ({{tr:tabīda}}) is the rare extinction word at the center of the denial. Its subjunctive form is governed by {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}), while {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) negates the speaker's estimation; its feminine agreement ties the perishing to the pointed garden itself. The root gives more than ordinary damage: it reaches toward total cessation, with the wasteland branch letting the denied outcome feel like a garden turned barren. The word is also isolated in the provided occurrence evidence, concentrating a uniquely sharp extinction vocabulary inside the owner's refusal. Structurally, the verb is enclosed by negated cognition before it and unbounded time after it.

topics.reason: The particle governs the subjunctive verb, and the feminine subject attachment ties it to the demonstrative that points back to the garden.

words.prose: {{ar:هَٰذِهِۦٓ}} ({{tr:hādhihi}}) turns the garden into a present, pointed object inside the quote. Its feminine form agrees with the garden and functions as the subject of {{ar:تَبِيدَ}} ({{tr:tabīda}}), so the claim is not about wealth in general or a vague situation. The demonstrative bridges the earlier entered object into the spoken subject of imperishability, making the same garden both the entered space and the entity whose extinction is denied. The attested {{ar:هَٰذِي}} ({{tr:hādhī}}) variant shifts the ending as apparatus while preserving the same feminine garden reference.

words.prose: {{ar:أَبَدًۭا}} ({{tr:abadan}}) closes the ayah with time made absolute. As an accusative adverbial, it modifies the denied perishing event rather than naming eternity as a separate noun. Under the negated cognition frame, its perpetuity range becomes never: the owner tries to shut every future opening through which the garden could vanish. That final position makes the arrogance climax in a temporal claim humans do not control, contrasting a mortal's private garden boast with divine granting of lasting garden permanence at 19:61-63 and with the divine sentence using the same temporal absolute at 18:57. The closing time-claim also resonates with the narrator's earlier indefinite diagnosis, binding verdict and boast in the ayah's cadence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence "entered his garden ... wronging himself ... said" at words 1-8.
baseline_models.mechanism: Spatial ingress into a tree-screened possession becomes inward enclosure: from inside what appears protective, the owner withholds from his own self the asset's perishability and voices the enclosure as security.

activation_trace.role: Literal ingress supplies the movement from outside to inside.
The tree-screened garden supplies an enclosure that can feel protective.
Withholding a right frames the harm as withholding truthful reckoning from the self.
The self as one's own identity locates both beneficiary and victim within him.
Voiced speech externalizes the judgment formed inside the enclosure.

changed_reading.before: An owner enters a prosperous garden and boasts that it will last.
changed_reading.after: Entry into the sheltered possession stages a cognitive enclosure: he treats what surrounds him as security and harms himself by voicing that enclosure as truth.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The clause "I do not think that this will perish, ever" at words 7-12.
baseline_models.mechanism: The utterance closes an uncertain outcome-space: perishing is negated while "ever" supplies limitless duration, so conjecture is made to function as a warranty.

activation_trace.role: Speech as belief or position makes the sentence a committed worldview, not a passing description.
An outcome that is not intrinsically secure supplies the uncertainty he suppresses.
Total going-away unto destruction supplies the excluded outcome.
Unbounded duration supplies the absolute horizon placed over the garden.

changed_reading.before: He is very confident that the garden will survive.
changed_reading.after: He converts a live, untrustworthy outcome into a private warranty by verbally excluding destruction from unlimited time.

context_deltas.mechanism: The gardens first give their yield without withholding anything; the owner then becomes the one who withholds what is due, and the deprived party is his own self. Material fidelity and human infidelity reverse roles.

activation_trace.role: The productive tree-screened gardens supply the material agent in the contrast.
Negated withholding marks the gardens as giving their produce without diminution.
Positive withholding transfers failure from the gardens to their owner.
The owner's own self identifies who is denied the due acknowledgment.

structural_cues: 18:33 negates z-l-m of the two gardens immediately before 18:35 predicates z-l-m of their owner.
Full yield precedes the owner's denial that the yielding system can end.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated z-l-m, undiminished yield, and self-directed wrong; I supply the reversal that he withholds truthful acknowledgment from himself. A live alternative is that 18:33 only describes quantitative shortfall, without personifying the gardens ethically.

changed_reading.before: He wrongs himself by holding an incorrect belief about his property.
changed_reading.after: The property fulfills its material due, but its owner fails the reciprocal due of truthful acknowledgment; the garden does not shortchange him, while he shortchanges his own self.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next utterance extends the same judgment into a two-branch no-loss hedge: either no final ending occurs, or any return ends in something better. Permanence and replacement are made to insure each other.

activation_trace.role: Repeated uncertain judgment carries the focus ayah's cognitive operator into the next claim.
Return to a prior source supplies the fallback branch of the hedge.
Beneficial superiority turns the fallback return into anticipated gain.
Turning toward a destination gives the imagined return an advantageous endpoint.
Unlimited duration supplies the first, no-ending branch of the hedge.

structural_cues: 18:36 immediately repeats the first-person negated z-n-n construction.
Denial of the Hour is followed by a conditional return and a claim of a better destination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies denial, conditional return, and expected improvement; I supply the insurance-like relation between them. A live alternative is escalating inconsistency rather than a consciously integrated hedge.

changed_reading.before: The speaker predicts that one garden will not perish.
changed_reading.after: The prediction is one half of a total no-loss worldview: he imagines himself protected both from ending and within any ending.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later admonition replays entry, garden, and speech but supplies a different utterance, one that locates the garden under will and strength beyond the owner. The focus statement becomes a substituted threshold speech-act.

activation_trace.role: Repeated ingress marks entry as the shared spatial threshold.
The same tree-screened possession fixes the repeated scene.
The explicit command to voice words supplies the alternative speech-act.
Will attached to the thing makes the possession contingent rather than self-securing.
Gathered strength relocates effective power outside the owner's possession.

structural_cues: The replacement utterance names will and power precisely where 18:35 names non-perishing duration.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lexical replay and an alternate utterance; I supply the threshold function, treating entry as the point where dependence should be voiced. A live alternative is a general correction delivered at entry, not a formal threshold practice.

changed_reading.before: His permanence claim happens to be spoken while he is in the garden.
changed_reading.after: His permanence claim occupies the exact speech slot where contingency should have been acknowledged; the wrong is not silence but substitution.

context_deltas.mechanism: The denied perishing is unpacked into a dependency cascade: footing loses grip, water drops beyond reach, yield is overwhelmed, expenditure becomes irrecoverable, and the trellised support system falls. "This" is not one durable object but a coupled material and financial system.

activation_trace.role: Going away unto destruction supplies the single outcome denied in the focus ayah.
A surface on which footing cannot hold removes the garden's stable ground.
Descent into depth removes accessible water from the productive system.
Overwhelming enclosure turns the apparent protective surround into a surround of destruction.
Money gone out in expenditure exposes the financial input now stranded in the loss.
Falling and collapse supply the visible failure state.
Grape trellising supplies the elevated support whose fall exposes structural dependence.

structural_cues: 18:40-42 move in order from ground to water to fruit, expenditure, and trellised supports.
The singular demonstrative in 18:35 is later resolved into multiple vulnerable components.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered failures; I supply the systems arrow that loss of ground and water propagates through yield, investment, and supports. A live alternative is a sequence of independent calamity images rather than a technical causal chain.

changed_reading.before: He denies a single catastrophic disappearance of the garden.
changed_reading.after: He denies the vulnerability of an entire dependency stack; perishing can occur by ordinary supports ceasing to hold, flow, repay, and stand.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the non-dominant q-w-l to q-l-l mapping and transfers later physical instability into speech. It remains anchored at the focus verb of saying and is reinforced by the later unstable surface, but downstream prose should label it an exploratory root resonance, not the lexical meaning of the verb.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The saying verb at word 6 immediately launches the permanence claim.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant mapping's trembling and motion image makes the firm utterance resonate with instability.
An outcome not secure in itself keeps uncertainty active beneath the assertion.
Later loss of physical footing gives the verbal trembling a visible contextual counterpart.

changed_reading.before: The spoken claim sounds grammatically and rhetorically firm.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the pronouncement already trembles at the root-mapping edge before the garden's ground is shown unable to hold.

strongest_changes: The exact z-l-m recurrence contrasts gardens that withhold none of their yield with an owner who withholds truthful reckoning from himself.
The repeated enter-garden-say triad at 18:39 recasts 18:35 as the wrong utterance at a threshold of dependence.
The later footing-water-yield-trellis cascade decomposes "this" from a permanent object into a vulnerable system.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah already joins enclosure, self-harm, voiced judgment, and eternity; context activates reversals in yield, speech, and infrastructure without requiring one harmonized reading.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the 18:33 z-l-m echo supports ethical personification or only a contrast with undiminished yield.
Whether the 18:36 continuation is a coherent no-loss hedge or merely escalating inconsistency.
The q-w-l to q-l-l outlier is branch-backed but intentionally form-distant.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **A provisional estimate is inflated into permanence.** `ء ب د` B001 (“enduring duration and permanence”) is governed by his `ظن`, structurally opposing God’s announced reversal of adornment into barrenness (18:7–8). The cave’s long stay and the final gardens show that duration is assigned, not inferred from present appearance. I infer that self-wrong consists in converting current abundance into evidence of independent perpetuity. Entry into the garden narrows his temporal horizon.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:98’s explicitly temporary barrier decisively corrected the owner’s inference from intact form to perpetuity.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The denied ruin already contains a waste-land image.** `ب ي د/B001` is perishing away, while `ب ي د/B002` is the open waste. The owner utters the negation inside the enclosed garden; exactly five ayat later, 18:40 imagines it becoming exposed, slippery ground, after 18:39 denies independent force. I infer that the dormant landscape branch gives material shape to the denied event. `تَبِيدَ` reads not only as temporal cessation but as enclosure reverting to bare waste.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:40 supplied the dormant landscape image exactly: the enclosed garden can become exposed, slippery waste.

baseline.text: Kendine haksızlık ederek bahçesine girdi ve, Bunun hiçbir zaman yok olacağını sanmıyorum, dedi.

findings.text: Bahçenin şimdiki görünüşünü bağımsız sonsuzluğun kanıtı saymak, geçici tahmini kalıcılığa şişirerek kişinin zaman ufkunu daraltır.
Yok olmayacağı söylenen bahçenin içinde, ileride ortaya çıkacak çorak alan imgesi daha inkar anında gizlice bulunur.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The immediate continuation extends his false supposition from the garden's permanence to denial of the Hour and an assumed better return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The unalterable revealed word stands over against the owner's unsupported personal prediction.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its permanent loss of success after coerced return is a distant contrast to the owner's claim that his present condition will never end.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It directly names a manifest wrongdoer against himself, clarifying the focus's self-wronging as a moral condition.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Granted everlasting abiding supplies the proper counterpart to the owner's self-asserted permanence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: God-granted eternal reward contrasts with the owner's unfounded claim that a worldly garden cannot perish.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A display of possession is identified as the Lord's favor and a test of gratitude, correcting the owner's possessive confidence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its warning against seeking worldly adornment frames the parable's garden as a test of the gaze and desire.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The refusal to wish for death because of prior wrongdoing has only a broad connection through wrongful action and an absolute claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It distinguishes the one who wrongs himself from more rightly directed servants, making that focus description morally substantive.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The companion directly corrects the owner at his garden: he should have attributed its existence and power to God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The hypocrites' false promise of never obeying anyone is another unreliable absolute assertion, though in a different setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Moses entering the city and the ensuing conflict do not clarify the garden owner's self-wronging or permanence claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The nearby declaration of truth, belief, disbelief, and punishment supplies the moral horizon for the owner's speech.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It portrays a false prediction that something will never happen, illuminating the owner's confident but baseless forecast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Striving benefits oneself, but the ayah does not materially specify the focus's wealth, permanence, or self-deception.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: After the garden's loss, the owner has neither a supporting group nor power to rescue himself, disproving his confidence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Divinely decreed everlasting punishment contrasts with the owner's imagined permanence for a worldly possession.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It closely repeats the pattern of receiving favor, claiming it as one's own, denying the Hour, and presuming a better return.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The next ayah contrasts the owner's self-deluding claim with God's preservation of the reward for genuine good action.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Eternal gardens are promised to faithful righteous people, distinguishing granted abiding from possessive presumption.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The destruction of a crop belonging to people who wrong themselves gives a close material image for the focus's vulnerable garden.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The local contrast supplies gardens of lasting reward rather than a worldly garden mistakenly thought indestructible.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The permanent exclusion of false accusers from testimony is a legal ruling unrelated to the focus's claim about his garden.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The ruined town and God's power over death challenge any inference that an apparent material state is beyond reversal.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It depicts people whose worldly effort is lost while they suppose it excellent, closely paralleling false self-assessment.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Faithful action is followed by God-granted everlasting gardens and provision, contrasting with the owner's temporal possession.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Thankfulness for received wisdom benefits the person, providing the fitting response absent from the garden owner's speech.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It begins the two-garden parable and establishes the setting in which the owner's claim is made.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Everlasting punishment for disobedience is only a broad contrast to the owner's asserted permanence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The believers reject a ruler's temporary worldly power, reinforcing that this worldly life is not the lasting measure.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The lasting abode whose inhabitants seek no change sharply contrasts with the owner's unfounded claim for his garden.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It presents enduring gardens as reward granted by the Lord to those who fear Him, not as a possession secured by wealth.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: Entering prison and the prisoners' dreams do not clarify the focus's central themes.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The full productivity and flowing river explain why the owner could mistake a prosperous garden for a permanent one.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It repeats the fear-driven refusal to wish for death, with only a broad link through wrongdoing and absolute language.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The distinction between recompense for evil and entry into the garden for believing righteous action corrects presumptive entitlement.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Gardens of Firdaws are prepared lodging for faith and righteous action, contrasting with a transient garden claimed as permanent.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's true promise of eternal gardens provides a direct contrast to the owner's unsupported claim about worldly permanence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The owner's boast of greater wealth and stronger followers supplies the social arrogance immediately behind his claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Revelation increasing believers in faith does not closely illuminate the owner's garden, beyond a general contrast in response to signs.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The warning against taking servants as protectors besides God anticipates the parable's exposure of misplaced reliance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its use of supposition occurs in a different confrontation and provides little beyond the verbal form of the owner's claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The companion identifies the owner's stance as disbelief in the Creator, giving the theological diagnosis of the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Entry into the garden follows faith and righteous deeds without injustice, not material advantage or self-assurance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The parable concludes that true authority, reward, and outcome belong to God alone, overturning the owner's confidence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The call to shared belief and notice of dissension do not materially clarify the garden owner's claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The companion's exclusive devotion to God directly counters the owner's failure to acknowledge his Lord.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The brother's decision to remain under a pledge is narratively and thematically remote from the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The garden's actual ruin and the owner's regret realize the destruction he had declared impossible.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Turning from the Lord's signs while forgetting prior deeds describes a wider pattern of self-wronging and persistent misguidance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The companion explicitly foresees the garden being reduced to barren, slippery ground, refuting the owner's permanence claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: People's confidence in favorable passage collapses under danger, showing how secure appearances can be suddenly overturned.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The possible disappearance of the garden's water exposes a basic resource as beyond the owner's control or recovery.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Unequal worldly rank and what people are given are presented as a divine test, not evidence of secure ownership.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Those who desire worldly life envy Qarun's visible splendor, paralleling the valuation that makes the garden persuasive.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The end of Moses's companionship concerns patience with hidden wisdom, not the owner's garden or claim of permanence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Demanding that a messenger possess a treasure or productive garden treats worldly wealth as proof of standing, a related false measure.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The rhetorical challenge to presumptuous hopes of entering bliss parallels confidence in a favorable outcome without its grounds.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The question about devotion to idols is too general to materially clarify the focus's garden and permanence claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The prohibition on worshipping Satan identifies misplaced obedience as an enemy-led path, broadly related to self-wronging.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The hoopoe's report of certain news has no substantive connection to the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Moses explicitly acknowledges that he wronged himself and seeks forgiveness, offering a repentant contrast to the owner's self-wronging.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Satan's lure of immortality through the forbidden tree closely parallels being seduced by a promise of unending possession.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: A mistaken supposition about whether people and jinn would lie about God has only a general link through false assumption.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The command never to repeat slander is a specific ethical ruling unrelated to the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The worldly life is made attractive to disbelievers, explaining how visible prosperity can be mistaken for true worth.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: A flourishing garden can be reduced by destructive wind and fire, directly challenging confidence in a garden's immunity from loss.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The attraction of wealth, children, livestock, and cultivated land is named as worldly enjoyment rather than the lasting destination.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Neither wealth nor children can avail their possessors before God, limiting the security the owner reads from possession.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Adam and his wife acknowledge that they wronged themselves and seek mercy, providing a repentant contrast to the owner's self-wronging.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth and children are explicitly a trial, supplying the evaluative frame for the owner's garden and social strength.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: When family, wealth, trade, and dwellings are loved above God, their apparent value becomes spiritually destructive.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth and children are not necessarily favor; they can be the means of distress in worldly life and punishment beyond it.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The repetition that wealth and children are a trial reinforces that abundance cannot demonstrate a secure outcome.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The life of this world is compared to vegetation that flourishes and is then suddenly reduced to stubble, closely matching the garden's vulnerability.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Those who seek only worldly life and its adornment receive its temporary return but lose their lasting share.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Preferring worldly life over the Hereafter diagnoses the distorted valuation behind treating a garden as the final horizon.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A secure and well-provided town is made to taste hunger and fear after ingratitude, showing prosperity can be withdrawn.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Whoever wants only the immediate world receives a limited allotment and then faces the Hereafter, opposing the owner's narrowed time horizon.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: When human beings receive favor they turn away arrogantly, a behavioral parallel to the owner's response to abundance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The parable of rain-fed vegetation becoming dry debris gives the chapter's direct general image for worldly transience.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth and children are worldly adornment, while enduring righteous deeds are better in reward and hope; it states the parable's governing contrast.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Worldly splendor given to others is a test and must not draw the eye away from the Lord's better and more lasting provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Every soul will taste death and both evil and good are tests, denying a horizon of unqualified worldly continuity.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth and children should not be read as proof that God is hastening good to their possessors.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The correction continues: those surrounded by wealth and children do not perceive the real meaning of that provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Deeds that look like water to the thirsty but prove empty provide a related image of deceptive appearances and failed expectation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Building as though one will live forever parallels the owner's attempt to project permanence from present material strength.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The Day when wealth and children do not benefit directly overturns the owner's reliance on property and social standing.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Only a sound heart benefits on that Day, supplying the moral alternative to possessions as security.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Whatever worldly goods are given are only enjoyment and adornment, while what is with God is better and more lasting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Qarun's exultant dependence on his great stores closely parallels the garden owner's confidence in accumulated wealth.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Qarun attributes his wealth to his own knowledge, a close counterpart to treating a received garden as self-secured.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The earth swallowing Qarun and his house demonstrates the abrupt defeat of material security and social self-rescue.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Observers learn that God expands and restricts provision, correcting their earlier wish for Qarun's worldly position.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Worldly life is diversion and play, while the real life is the final abode; this directly corrects the owner's temporal valuation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The worldly life and the deceiver must not mislead people about God, a direct warning against false security.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Affluent elites commonly reject warning, providing a social pattern into which the garden owner's self-assurance fits.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The claim that wealth and children guarantee immunity from punishment closely matches the owner's material confidence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth and children do not bring a person near to God; faith and righteous action, not possession, determine recompense.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The worldly life is not to deceive people about God, identifying the general error embodied by the owner's prediction.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Attachment to splendid possessions can make one neglect remembrance of the Lord, a related failure of valuation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Water produces thriving crops that later wither and become debris, another explicit image of the garden's impermanence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: After receiving favor, a person claims it was given because of personal knowledge, paralleling possessive self-deception.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Worldly life is only temporary enjoyment while the Hereafter is the permanent home, directly negating the owner's horizon.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: When given favor, people turn away arrogantly; this closely describes the owner's posture within abundance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Whatever people receive is only enjoyment of worldly life, whereas what is with God is better and more lasting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Even lavish houses and material display are described as mere enjoyment of worldly life, not lasting distinction.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Ornaments and visible luxury continue the argument that worldly splendor is not evidence of final favor.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: All such adornment is worldly enjoyment, while the Hereafter belongs to the God-conscious.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Those who exhausted their good things in worldly life are confronted with the failure of that worldly valuation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Worldly life is play and diversion, and wealth is tested rather than held out as a permanent possession.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Worldly life is adornment, rivalry in wealth and children, and vegetation that later becomes debris; it is a comprehensive parallel to the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: People are told not to exult over what they receive, directly opposing the owner's boastful confidence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Protection from one's own greed is the mark of success, supplying a moral contrast to possessive attachment.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth and children must not distract from God's remembrance, naming the spiritual danger of abundance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth and children are a trial, again denying that their presence proves stability or favor.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The owners of the garden are tested through a garden that is later devastated, making this a close narrative counterpart.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: After the garden's loss, its owners hope their Lord will replace it with better, the opposite of claiming the present garden cannot perish.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth is confessed not to have availed its possessor, reducing material accumulation to failed security.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Abundant wealth is listed among gifts bestowed on a person who nevertheless resists gratitude and warning.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Despite extensive gifts, the person still demands more, exposing acquisitiveness rather than secure sufficiency.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Love of the immediate world is contrasted with neglect of the Hereafter, directly naming the focus's shortened horizon.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Those who love the immediate world leave behind a weighty Day, another direct contrast to the owner's outlook.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Transgression and preference for worldly life are given as a path with a final consequence, clarifying the moral stakes of the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The resulting destination is contrasted with worldly preference, redirecting the claim of lasting security to the final abode.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Preferring worldly life is explicitly rebuked, matching the owner's valuation of present possession.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The Hereafter is declared better and more lasting, providing the direct correction to asserted worldly permanence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A person mistakes expanded provision for honor, the same faulty inference from material abundance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Intense love of wealth identifies the desire that can make material abundance appear decisive.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The self-sufficient person who denies the better outcome provides a broader portrait of the owner's posture.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Human beings transgress when they see themselves as self-sufficient, closely diagnosing the owner's confidence.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Seeing oneself as self-sufficient is the stated cause of that transgression, directly relevant to self-wronging through possession.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Intense love of wealth describes the attachment that makes a garden appear to guarantee the future.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Rivalry in accumulation distracts people, directly challenging the owner's boast in wealth and followers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: That rivalry lasts only until the graves, cutting off the imagined permanence of accumulated worldly goods.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The hoarder and counter of wealth is a close moral parallel to possessive confidence in material accumulation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: He thinks his wealth will make him immortal, the Qur'an's closest verbal and conceptual counterpart to the owner's claim.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Abu Lahab's wealth and gains do not avail him, providing a concise outcome-based rejection of material security.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: Supposition Is Defeated by Exhaustive Accounting
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Surface-based estimation misclassifies scale, state, durability, and value, whereas exhaustive count or final disclosure fixes what the object actually is.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The contrast joins visual illusion, economic confidence, false allegiance, and skilled labor under one epistemic failure.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Possession, Allegiance, and Craft Generate False Self-Estimates
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A garden owner predicts permanence, false allies are assumed usable, and lost workers suppose their production excellent.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: unsupported conjecture `ظ ن ن:B003/m01`; imagined permanence `ء ب د:B001/m01`; supposition `ح س ب:B002/m01`; adopted dependence `ء خ ذ:B010/m01`; chosen ally `و ل ي:B004/m01`; skilled craft `ص ن ع:B002/m01`; lost course `ض ل ل:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 18:35-36 (garden permanence and return estimated from possession); 18:102 (allies presumed viable); 18:104 (lost labor supposed well made)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Each estimate treats present control as evidence of future or final value. Disclosure separates confidence in the work or support from its actual standing.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: A Fixed Promise Ends Temporary Arrangements
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Concealment, delay, material protection, and claims of permanence remain subordinate to a divinely fixed temporal boundary.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sleep, a garden, delayed punishment, a rampart, and final lodging are all evaluated by who controls their duration.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Asserted Permanence Is Distinguished from Granted Abiding
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: The garden owner's forecast that his possession will never perish is set against promised reward and final lodging whose abiding does not depend on possession.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: imagined permanence `ء ب د:B001/m01`; unsupported conjecture `ظ ن ن:B003/m01`; abiding residence `خ ل د:B001/m01`; guest provision and lodging `ن ز ل:B005/m01`; change of place or state `ح و ل:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 18:3 (promised abiding reward); 18:35-36 (garden and return assigned permanence by conjecture); 18:107-108 (abiding lodging with no desired transfer)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Duration is not established by confidence or enclosure. True abiding is received as an outcome, while asserted permanence collapses with the object that was expected to guarantee it.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, temel anlamı dışarıdan içeriye geçiş olarak kuruyor; yerin yanı sıra zaman ve işe girmeyi, ayrıca bir şeyi içeri sokmayı ve aşamalı biçimde içine ilerlemeyi de bu çekirdeğe bağlıyor.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal içeriye geçişi temel alır; gizli iç yüz, içten bozukluk ve kalıplaşmış eşlik kullanımları ayrı dallarda kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın içeri girme çekirdeğini, bir başkasını içeri sokan ettirgen kullanımdan ve özel türemiş kullanımlardan açıkça ayırır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi ya da şey bir yerin, zamanın veya işin dışından içine geçer. Aynı çekirdek, bir başkasını içeri sokma ve bir şeyin içine aşamalı biçimde ilerleme yönleriyle genişler.

facets.statement: Bir kişi ya da şey dışarıdaki bir konum veya durumdan içerideki konum veya duruma geçer.
Ettirgen kullanım, başka bir kişi ya da şeyin içeriye geçmesini sağlamayı bildirir.
Geçiş yer, zaman veya iş alanında gerçekleşebilir ve kimi kullanımda azar azar ilerleyen bir süreç olarak sunulur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım, dışarıdan içeriye yönelen geçişi esas alır; yer, zaman ve iş alanlarını, ettirgen içeri sokmayı ve aşamalı ilerlemeyi bu esasın düzenli görünümleri sayar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yer, zaman ya da bir işe katılma alanında dışarıdan içeriye geçişi ve bunun ettirgen karşılığını birlikte anlatmak için uygundur.
